 Description: 
 Amazing electronic model from Canon factory: A Canon Typemate # 10 (not a Typestar). 
At first sight, you can say "another Typestar", but looking further there are differences between the Typemate and its siblings:  
There is no external platen knob; 
Near all its levers are sliding mode on this model; 
The ribbon cassette is different from the Typestar ribbon cassette; 
Its overall shape is reduced in comparison with Typestars. 
Is hard to find any kind of information about the Canon Typemate on the internet (text or images, my search results were a complete failure) 
Despite the ink in the cassette ribbon being faint, I manage to get a Typeface Specimen Sample.

 Description: 
 A lesser model than my Typestar 5,  this is another portable electronic typewriter made by Canon in the eighties. As its bigger brother it types taking its energy from mains or by four D batteries.  
The reason to buy this model, considering the Typestar 5 is a little advanced than the Typestar 2?: Weird but simple enough. The inking method is provided by a cassette very hard to find nowadays. And this one was cheaper than the market price of just ONE Canon cassette, and cames with its own cassette in place, PLUS other two unused original Canon cassettes!!!!. 
A spare parts bargain, isn't it? :-))

 Description: 
 I do not think this is a typewriter. I submit it to the database as an edge case, to help clarify what is and what isn’t. The keyboard and the portability make it look somewhat like a typewriter but it is really a computer with built-in printer. 
 
There is a continuum from electric-assisted-mechanical typewriters through electricity-required machines (e.g., Selectrics, which could not work with finger pressure) through the wedges with their electronics-controlled mechanical hammer (and which could be computer-driven) to this, which is computer-driven and has finally eliminated impact altogether. The last vestige of mechanical parts are the cables and pulleys that move the thermal printhead; although the keys do move, they could just as well be capacitance sensors so that possible link doesn’t count. It does use an “ink” source and plain paper, but so does ‘most every other computer printer. This looks like a wedge, so we might be tempted to call it a typewriter just by extending the (questionable?) courtesy by which we call the wedges typewriters ... nah. 
 
This might not even be able to place one character at a time, a universal hallmark of a typewriter. Maybe it can, but I don’t know how without an instruction manual---another difference from a real typewriter. 
 
If you all want to delete this from the database, fine with me.

 Description: 
 As I was looking to purchase and try a thermal electronic typewriter, I came across two machines on Facebook Marketplace - this Canon Typestar 220-II and a Brother EP-150. I decided to go for the Brother because it was the only one with Greek typeface and also for its white color, as black devices are not something I like. Despite all these, the Canon seems to be a nice machine, so I decided to add it here for our viewing pleasure. It has a spell checker, lcd display, types in four different styles and can also add little drawings to your documents (cute!!).

 Description: 
 And now an unblemished (and certainly close to brand new condition) Typestar 3, the little Canon ultraportable electronic you can use even without ribbon (just by using thermal paper to print in). 
The differences between the Typestar/Typemaster Canon line do exist (albeit they are little ones). 
A visible difference between this model 3 and its siblings is the presence of a collapsible transportation handle. 
In a few days more, with four D batteries (or a transformer, which I lack now) the Typeface Specimen Sample :-)

 Description: 
 My go-to Typestar 5 II in great working condition. I just fixed a non-responsive Return key by opening her up gently and cleaning all the contact points on the keys and board with alcohol. Worked like a charm! I found some excellent Thermal Receipt paper from Amazon that works great when you remove the print cartridge. I find myself using it for longer Twitter messages and fast writing. I love that I can use my iPad Pro 2021 to scan and create a copy in Word or Google Docs. I’m never parting with this typewriter.
